A Partner Development Manager (PDM) at AWS is a go-to-market and relationship role focused on growing revenue and customer adoption through strategic partners (ISVs, MSPs, SIs, resellers, marketplaces). The job mixes business development, partner strategy, program execution, and cross-team coordination to enable partners to build, market, sell, and deploy on AWS.

Core responsibilities
- Partner strategy & planning: develop joint business plans and GTM strategies with assigned partners (ISVs, SIs, MSPs, VARs). Align partner goals to AWS priorities and customer segments.
- Pipeline & revenue growth: drive partner-sourced pipeline, influence partner-led and co-sell opportunities, and hit revenue / ARR / consumption targets.
- Enablement & onboarding: help partners with technical enablement, AWS programs (APN, ISV Accelerate, SaaS Factory, MSP programs), certifications, solution validation (Well-Architected, security/compliance).
- Co-selling & go-to-market: coordinate with AWS account teams, solution architects, marketing, and partner marketing to run joint campaigns, webinars, events, and field engagements.
- Relationship management: be the primary AWS contact for partner leadership, build executive-level relationships, and escalate issues to remove blockers.
- Program & product feedback: surface partner feedback to AWS product, services, and partner programs teams to improve offerings and incentives.
- Metrics & reporting: track KPIs such as pipeline creation, partner-influenced revenue, customer wins, certification counts, solution listings, and marketplace listings.

Day-to-day activities
- Meeting with partner execs/product teams to align on roadmap and GTM.
- Running partner business review (PBR) and updating joint plans and commitments.
- Coordinating internal AWS resources (Account Managers, Solutions Architects, marketing).
- Reviewing partner pipelines and qualification of partner-sourced deals.
- Driving enablement sessions, technical reviews, proof-of-concept planning.
- Tracking program milestones (APN tiers, ISV Accelerate approval, marketplace listings).
- Preparing executive summaries, status reports, and forecasting.

Key skills & qualifications
- Strong relationship building and influencing skills; comfortable at executive level.
- Sales acumen: experience in quota-driven or revenue-impact roles; understanding of sales cycles and forecasting.
- Cloud knowledge: familiarity with AWS services, architecture patterns, pricing/billing, and cloud value propositions. Certifications helpful but not always required.
- Technical fluency: able to discuss architectures, integrations, and partner solutions with technical teams.
- Program & project management: run multi-stakeholder programs, coordinate deadlines, and execute campaigns.
- Analytical and data-driven: track KPIs, analyze partner performance, and optimize efforts.
- Communication: clear written and verbal communication for executive presentations and technical coordination.

Typical metrics / success measures
- Partner-influenced pipeline and closed revenue (ARR, bookings).
- Number of qualified opportunities and customer wins.
- Partner enablement outcomes: certifications, validated solutions, marketplace listings.
- Partner satisfaction and retention; partner program tier advancement.
- Velocity and conversion rates of partner-led deals.

How it differs from related roles
- vs. Account Manager / Territory Sales: PDM focuses on partner relationships and enabling partner-sourced revenue rather than direct named-account quotas (though PDMs often influence revenue targets).
- vs. Partner Solutions Architect: PDM leans more on GTM, business development and program management; PSAs are more hands-on technical enablement.
- vs. Channel/Alliance Manager at other companies: AWS PDMs work within AWS’ partner programs, with deep focus on cloud economics, APN, and co-sell motions.

Background & typical experience
- 3–8+ years in partner/channel roles, business development, tech sales, or alliances.
- Experience with cloud/solutions or SaaS companies preferred; knowledge of enterprise customers.
- MBA or relevant degree can help but isn’t required.

Tips to succeed
- Be proactive in creating joint business plans with measurable milestones and mutual commitments.
- Build strong relationships with AWS account teams and partner leadership; be the “glue” that removes blockers.
- Focus on high-impact partners and opportunities—prioritize where technical fit and GTM overlap.
- Learn enough technical detail to speak credibly with solution architects and customers.
- Use AWS partner programs and incentives effectively (co-sell designation, ISV Accelerate, Marketplace, funding programs).

Sample resume bullets
- Built joint GTM plan with ISV partner resulting in $5M partner-influenced ARR within 12 months; enabled 15 customer POCs and marketplace listing.
- Drove partner enablement program that increased partner-certified solution architects by 60% and accelerated deal velocity by 40%.
- Orchestrated co-sell motion across AWS field teams and partner, closing 10 enterprise deals in 6 months.

Interview prep: common questions
- Describe a partner GTM you built from scratch. What were the results?
- How do you prioritize partners and opportunities?
- Walk me through how you would enable an ISV to migrate and commercialize a SaaS product on AWS Marketplace.
- How do you handle conflicts between partner commitments and AWS account team priorities?
- Give an example of influencing a technical solution and coordinating a multi-team sale.

If you want, I can:
- Draft a tailored resume summary or bullets for this role.
- Create a 30/60/90-day onboarding plan for a PDM at AWS.
- Prepare answers to common interview questions with sample talking points. Which would be most useful?
